The girl was hospitalized, where she died. The girl’s family had not previously come to the attention of the police and was not subject to preventive monitoring
Regarding the child’s death, investigators opened criminal proceedings under Clause 2, Part 2, Article 115 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine, marked as “suicide.” As part of the investigation, the necessary examinations have been ordered, and all circumstances that could have preceded the tragedy are being established.
Police also reported that on August 9, a video of a conflict between minors that took place in an unfinished building was circulated on social media. The video shows one of the girls hitting another. Police established that one of the participants in the conflict was the 11-year-old girl who subsequently died by suicide.
According to preliminary information, the incident occurred approximately 20–21 days before the child’s death. No statements or reports regarding this conflict had been received by the police at the time it occurred. Regarding the incident recorded on video, law enforcement officers also launched criminal proceedings under Article 126 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine (beatings and torture).
Police are currently establishing all participants and witnesses to the conflict and clarifying its causes and circumstances. As part of the investigation, they are also checking whether the events recorded on video could have been connected to the child’s death. The investigation is ongoing. Final conclusions regarding the circumstances of the child’s death and a possible connection with other events will be made based on the results of a set of investigative actions and examinations
The Main Department of the National Police in Cherkasy region told a UNN journalist that the necessary measures to establish all the circumstances are still underway.

Canadian airline WestJet agrees to settle flight attendants’ sexual harassment class action
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:40:36 UTC
23:40:36 KST

The Canadian airline WestJet has agreed to pay C$4.5m (£2.4m) to settle a decade-long sexual harassment class action lawsuit levelled by its female flight attendants, who alleged the company failed to maintain a safe workplace.
The suit followed allegations by Mandalena Lewis, a former flight attendant, that a pilot had sexually assaulted her and a colleague, but that WestJet kept the pilot flying, thereby putting other employees at risk.
A British Columbia judge on Monday approved the terms of the settlement, which were finalised on 22 June after months of negotiation. The payment will be distributed among the 3,452 flight attendants in the class action after expenses are removed, including legal fees.
WestJet agreed to hire a third-party to conduct a workplace inquiry that will examine the prevalence of harassment, the extent of underreporting and how reporting systems can be made more effective.
The suit had called on WestJet to implement mandatory anti-harassment training for pilots, along with an admission of wrongdoing and an admission of a breach of employee contract. None were included in the settlement.
Lewis filed the initial class action against the airline in April 2016. She said she was dismayed by the results, especially given that two years ago WestJet paid out $12.5m in a baggage fee class action, nearly three times the amount agreed to in the sexual harassment suit.
“I’m glad it’s over … but I’m just exhausted. I’m shaking my head,” she said, adding that she was advised the amount was the most that could be achieved given that legal expenses were piling up.
Under BC law, the suit included all female flight attendants who worked for the company between 4 April 2014 and 28 February 2021, because Lewis’s suit alleged that all of them had their contracts violated by WestJet during that period because its employee policy promised that the workplace would be free from harassment.
The suit claimed WestJet broke its policy by not taking enough steps to address reports of assault or to prevent harassment in the first place.
Lewis said she was sexually assaulted by a WestJet pilot while on a layover in Hawaii in 2010 when she was 25 years old. In court documents, she said the same pilot had also assaulted another flight attendant in 2008.
Though she reported the assault to WestJet, the pilot remained at the company and Lewis was eventually fired in 2016 for “gross insubordination”, according to court documents submitted by WestJet that year, which she and her legal team allege was retaliation for trying to hold the airline accountable internally.
She said she abandoned an individual civil claim and instead created the class action after learning other flight attendants had also experienced harassment.
Lewis said she reported the assault to police in Maui but alleges WestJet rerouted the pilot so he would not face questioning in Hawaii.
She said fellow members of the class action suit were also disappointed with the result. Eight of them had already asked the province’s supreme court not to approve the settlement in February when some of the details first emerged, citing a low payout and a lack of accountability by WestJet.
“We didn’t get justice here,” said Lewis.
The case garnered national attention for exposing pilot behaviour toward female flight attendants and the vulnerability of the scores of young women who have historically been the target demographic for the job.
A 2018 survey of more than 3,500 flight attendants by the US Association of Flight Attendants found that 68% had experienced sexual harassment in their careers while only 7% had reported an incident to their employer.
WestJet did not respond to questions about Lewis’s claims of assault, and the allegations that it failed to keep the workplace free of harassment and does not properly investigate alleged sexual assaults.
In a statement, the company said it was “pleased to have reached a mutually agreed upon settlement”. It said: “We are committed to strengthening our operations and training, focused on the safety and wellbeing of all WestJetters and we are focused on advancing a culture of empowerment.”

First Osprey nesting pair in Switzerland in 112 years
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:39:26 UTC
23:39:26 KST

First Osprey nesting pair in Switzerland in 112 years
Eleven years after the launch of a project to reintroduce the osprey in Switzerland, a pair of these migratory birds has returned to nest for the first time since 1914.
Three chicks hatched in the spring between May 25 and 29, reveals Wendy Strahm, coordinator of the reintroduction project run by the association Nos Oiseaux, formerly the Romandy Society for the Study and Protection of Birds. The exact location of the nest, situated in the region of the lakes of Neuchâtel, Bienne and Morat, will not be disclosed.
The last documented breeding of the osprey in Switzerland dates back 112 years. The species subsequently disappeared completely due to poachers and egg collectors.
Once they reach adulthood, at around three to four years of age, Ospreys instinctively return to breed in the region where they first took flight.
Between 2015 and 2020,66 chicks were imported from nests, mainly in Norway and Germany. Housed in aviaries, they were reared without any direct contact with humans.
All three chicks survived
This method of translocation – the movement of animals or plants from one place to another as part of species conservation projects – has already proven its effectiveness in other parts of Europe since 1996. A male marked with a numbered ring returned to nest in the Three Lakes region of the Western Plateau. The female, which is unringed, is of unknown origin.
The pair had already been spotted in the summer of 2025, when the female was still immature. After spending the winter apart in Africa, the two birds of prey returned. As hoped, they have taken up residence in the nest identified in 2025, situated on one of the thirty platforms set up in the Three Lakes region by the association’s volunteers. The female laid her first egg on April 19.
Such a success on the very first attempt is exceptional, all the more so as the spring turned out to be particularly cold and rainy. Two females and one male survived.
The next crucial stage for the young ospreys will be their migration to Africa, which is expected to take place by the end of the month. According to statistics, the mortality rate among young migrants reaches 80%.
Nos Oiseaux also hopes that the first pair of ospreys to return to breed in Switzerland since 1914 will return again in 2027.

The Israeli military failed in an attempt on Wednesday to remove occupied West Bank settlers who for days have blockaded Palestinian homes, an eyewitness and an AFP photographer reported.
The siege began on Sunday, when a group of settlers set up a makeshift tent near houses in the Palestinian village of Qusra, just south of Nablus, blocking essential supplies from entering.

Israel's defense chiefs rethink Gaza, Iran, Lebanon strategy three years into war - exclusive
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:39:02 UTC
23:39:02 KST

Standing two months away from the three-year anniversary of the start of the Israel-Hamas War, The Jerusalem Post has recently interviewed and spoken to top current and former defense officials, some of whom rarely speak to the media, to provide a broader view of where Israel stands on all of the military fronts.
Some major points remain under serious debate, while some points have hardened into a new consensus.
Regarding the broader consensus points, from Right to Left, top Israeli defense officials believe the country must maintain some kind of security zone in Gaza, Lebanon, and Syria for years to come.
Defense officials back long-term Gaza security zone
The Post understands that this remains true despite recent deals with Hamas in Gaza and the Lebanese government, as well as rising pressure from the US on those fronts and with Syria for Israeli withdrawals.
In contrast, there is disagreement between top defense officials about how to handle US pressure and how much to bend on some related withdrawal issues in order to maintain broader American support.
For example, the Post has learned that a majority of top Israeli defense officials are in favor of allowing the Palestinian Authority to take over Gaza from Hamas, and criticize Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for being an obstacle to this process.
They would prefer moving forward with the PA more rapidly than Netanyahu has, though there is a minority that supports the prime minister’s insistence on the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) as a sort of pressure point on the PA-connected officials to have to answer to the US Board of Peace.
Moving forward with the PA or NCAG is preferred despite heavy doubts that they will fully succeed at displacing Hamas as the main military power in Gaza.
Rather, they support giving the PA or NCAG a larger role in Gaza regardless of how much disarming Hamas succeeds and regardless of how long the process is drawn out.
There are also disagreements about how much Israel should be willing to withdraw from Gaza in exchange for Hamas carrying out partial disarming and partial delegating of political powers.
While a minority wish to hold on to maximum territory in Gaza, a majority are willing to withdraw to a smaller security zone, stating that the exact percentage is less important than keeping the high ground at each portion of the Strip, the Post has learned.
For example, the Post understands that the area around Shejaia requires the IDF to be deep into Gaza to maintain a useful buffer zone, whereas in Rafah, the military could control much less territory than it does now and still have an excellent vantage point to foresee and prevent any Hamas attempt to push into Israel.
In northern Gaza, there are ridges and hills from Netiv Haasara on the Israeli side which straddle parts of Beit Hanoun and other areas, which need to remain under Israeli control, but whether the total percentage of Israeli-controlled territory is 70%, 53%, around 30% or closer to 15% is less important than these on-the-ground realities.
If Hamas makes partial concessions, many Israeli defense officials are willing to make partial withdrawals, provided the high ground is maintained in a Gaza buffer zone.
These officials would insist on keeping such a zone for many years into the future because they do not believe that Gazan society is likely to change its hostile attitude toward Israel even if Hamas does some partial disarming and the PA or NCAG gain new political powers.
Israeli officials are skeptical of Lebanese army's ability to counter Hezbollah
Likewise, a majority of Israeli defense officials do not believe that the IDF needs to control the 10 kilometers or more of Lebanese territory it currently holds, but this is not because they have any faith in the Lebanese military versus Hezbollah.
Rather, even those Israeli defense officials who are quicker to endorse partial withdrawals from Lebanon to a smaller security zone have little faith that the Lebanese army taking control of “pilot” areas is anything more than a public relations effort, the Post has learned.
There is a spirited disagreement, the Post understands, about whether the daring new diplomatic engagement by the Lebanese government with Israel can have any real strategic impact on the threat that Hezbollah poses to Israel.
Some believe that with the Lebanese government’s public backing, Israel can reduce the Hezbollah threat, while some believe that the government is mostly irrelevant, noting that Lebanese President Joseph Aoun had been ready to meet with Netanyahu, then canceled out of fear of assassination.
'War between wars' remains part of Israel's defense strategy
Another broad area of consensus is for Israel to maintain a “war between wars” on all fronts, regularly performing attacks when necessary, which will prevent all enemies bordering Israel from increasing their strategic capacity to threaten Israel, the Post understands.
There is a debate within the defense establishment about how far to go with such attacks, and whether to dial back such attacks during periods when the US believes it is making diplomatic progress.
Some defense officials worry more that pausing the war between wars could make it harder to restart it when necessary, while some are more worried about losing American support when support for Israel globally has hit historic lows.
Defense establishment resists major Syria withdrawal
Regarding Syria, almost no one in the Israeli defense establishment wants to withdraw much from Syria, despite a recent push by Washington on the issue, the Post has noted.
Despite zero attacks by Syria on Israel since Syrian leader Ahmad al-Sharaa took power in December 2024, Israeli defense officials see how he has treated and massacred some of his own Syrian minority groups and believe he remains a product of al-Qaeda.
They mostly believe that his reluctance to attack Israel is an extended tactical delay because he has not yet fully taken control over his own existing territory.
Many of them regard Syria as a serious potential future danger since there is no formal mechanism for preventing the new Syrian army from growing its heavy weapons, including tanks and fighter jets.
Recent reports have suggested that Turkey will help Syria rebuild much of what Israel bombed in December 2024 when the Assad regime fell.
Defense officials reassess Israel's strategic position on Iran
Moving on to Iran, a majority of Israeli defense officials believe Israel’s strategic position was better off after the June 2025 operation than it is now after the early 2026 operation, the Post has learned.
While initially current IDF officials talked about high achievements in destroying Iran’s military capacities in terms of missiles, drones, and rebuilding its threat capacities, many are aghast that Tehran now has the US deterred due to the Straits of Hormuz crisis.
Further, they are worried about America preventing Israel from attacking Iran in the future if needed, whereas there was no such question after June 2025, since Washington was less involved.
Also, following the early 2026 operation, the Islamic Republic succeeded in reestablishing a connection between the Iranian and Hezbollah fronts, which Jerusalem had succeeded in cutting off in June 2025.
In addition, Iran has now had months to recover from the attacks, and Israeli defense officials are critical of US President Donald Trump for failing to attack sufficiently to maintain pressure on Tehran.
Israeli defense officials split over future Iran nuclear deal
Besides those consensus issues, there is a split about any future deal with Iran.
Some Israeli defense officials insist that there be no deal unless Iran gives up uranium enrichment for an extended period of years.
Others believe that Trump has made it clear that he will not enforce this position, and believe that Jerusalem must be more realistic, pushing for some least bad scenarios compared to worse ones.
For example, some Israeli defense officials would support a deal with Iran, given that Trump seems very committed to such a deal, which allowed a significant volume of centrifuges as long as the amount of enriched uranium was close to zero.
Alternatively, they could live with a small amount of enriched uranium at low levels if there were close to zero centrifuges.
The key would be that Iran would not be able to have significant amounts of centrifuges and enriched uranium at the same time, because one without the other makes a nuclear bomb impossible in the short and medium term.
They would also insist, the Post has learned, on much tougher nuclear inspections than under the 2015 JCPOA nuclear deal, such as anytime, anywhere inspections, as well as a ban on nuclear metallurgy weapons group activities.
None of this would eliminate the Iranian nuclear threat, but it would push back the threat farther than the JCPOA did and farther than the current situation.
Most Israeli defense officials are currently scratching their heads about how to prevent Iran from manufacturing a large new volume of ballistic missiles, since this is not even on Trump’s radar, but they at least believe the 2025 and 2026 operations bought Israel some time on this issue.

Queenstown, Tromsø, and Bariloche: These are the best cities for a coolcation this summer
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:38:31 UTC
23:38:31 KST

This new index looks at climate relief, accessibility, value and visitor experience to highlight the best overall coolcation destinations.
It may only be the third hottest year on record, but it sure feels like the summer heatwaves are never ending.
As temperatures rise to unbearable levels, more and more of us are swapping the Mediterranean for the Baltic Sea, or seeking relief further afield.
If you’re struggling to settle on a destination, we have good news, as Holafly has just released its Global Cool Escape Index.
Based on factors including climate relief, accessibility, traveller interest, visitor experience and value, the ranking aims to share the best coolcation spots overall, rather than the places that are actually the coldest temperature-wise.
The eSIM provider shared a general ranking, as well as specific rankings for Brits, Germans and Spaniards, all of which take into account airport connectivity.
Overall, the best coolcation spot is (drumroll please): Queenstown in New Zealand.
As it’s winter in the southern hemisphere, the resort town on the shores of Lake Wakatipu has daily mean temperatures of just 5.2°C. We would really welcome that right now…
Next on the overall ranking was Tromsø in Norway. As it’s north of the Arctic Circle, the town experiences the midnight sun phenomenon each year from around 20 May until 22 July, and after that the sun will still set pretty late in the evening.
Third place went to Argentina’s Bariloche. Located in the foothills of the Patagonian Andes, the city is a popular choice for skiers.
The top 10 coolcation spots for summer
- Queenstown, New Zealand
- Tromsø, Norway
- Bariloche, Argentina
- Helsinki, Finland
- Anchorage, United States
- Reykjavik, Iceland
- San Francisco, United States
- Banff, Canada
- Cape Town, South Africa
- Zermatt, Switzerland
When it comes to specific suggestions for UK travellers, Cape Town in South Africa is number one, followed by Chamonix in France, then overall index-topper Queenstown, with Innsbruck in Austria and Zermatt in Switzerland following behind.
For Germans, Innsbruck was the number one coolcation destination, followed by Cape Town, Zermatt, Chamonix, and Bariloche in Argentina.
Finally, Spaniards should be headed to Bariloche, and if they can’t make it there, Chamonix is a good runner-up, as is Cape Town, Zermatt, or Reykjavik in Iceland.

German Lawmakers Warn Berlin’s Russian House May Be an Intelligence Hub
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:38:11 UTC
23:38:11 KST

- Category
- World
German Lawmakers Warn Berlin’s Russian House May Be an Intelligence Hub
Lawmakers from Germany's Christian Democratic Union (CDU), the Greens, and the Free Democratic Party (FDP) are demanding the closure of the Russian House in Berlin, which they suspect is being used as a center for espionage.
The dispute was reported by Deutsche Welle (DW) on August 12, as pressure built on the German government to shut the state-linked cultural institution.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Roderich Kiesewetter, a CDU member of the Bundestag and its foreign policy specialist, argued that the site had abandoned its cultural role. In an August 11 interview with Welt TV, he characterized it as "a hub which is probably packed with intelligence equipment" and populated by people hostile to Germany. "This house is a symbol of our weakness and Russian influence," he declared.
Sara Nanni, a Greens lawmaker focused on defense, voiced similar suspicions. She pointed to unusual mobile and GPS signals that, in her view, may indicate powerful transmitting equipment inside the building.
Nanni recalled that her party had tried without success to close the Russian House under the previous government, and framed the current refusal to act as "submission" to the Kremlin. She warned that the Russian leader, Vladimir Putin, exploits such hesitancy for provocations, citing a drone attack the previous week in Leipzig that targeted a Ukrainian cargo aircraft.
Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann, an FDP member of the European Parliament, alleged that staff at the Russian House were involved in "coordination of cyberattacks and recruitment of spies."
"In the very center of Berlin sits an enemy of freedom, and we simply watch," she remarked, insisting that Germany "cannot allow such a degree of naivety." She urged the government to terminate the cultural cooperation treaty with Russia, which expires at the end of the year.
The Russian House officially functions as a cultural center in the German capital. In recent months, however, reports have surfaced suggesting that Russian intelligence services may be using the institution as cover.
The German government has resisted the calls, explaining that shutting the Russian House would force Berlin to break existing agreements with Moscow that also govern the Goethe-Institut's operations in the Russian capital.
"These two institutions are directly connected, and any further measures regarding one of them will immediately cause consequences for the other," Foreign Ministry spokesman Martin Giese told a DW correspondent at a Berlin press conference on August 10.
Concerns over Russian intelligence activity conducted under official cover in Germany have sharpened in recent months. Since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, Germany has expelled roughly 400 Russian citizens, including more than 80 diplomats assessed to be intelligence officers working under diplomatic cover. The Russian embassy in Berlin has itself come to be regarded as a hub for espionage and political influence operations.

The extinguishing of seven fires in ecosystems across the Kyiv, Lviv and Cherkasy regions is ongoing in Ukraine, UNN reports, citing the State Emergency Service of Ukraine.
Details
According to rescuers, the fire has engulfed nearly 15 hectares of forest floor and peatlands.

▪Kyiv region: 3 fires were localized in the exclusion zone over a total area of 3.5 hectares;

Nearly 80 firefighters and 14 units of State Emergency Service equipment are involved in the operation.
In total, 293 fires in ecosystems broke out across Ukraine over the past day, covering an area of more than 180 hectares.

Officers suspect the tobacco products were manufactured at an illegal factory operating in Latvia for several years.
In total, approximately 412,000 packs of cigarettes were found in the trailer, with a market value, including taxes, of 2.1 million euros.
A pre-trial investigation into the illegal possession of excise goods has been launched, led by prosecutors from the Kaunas Regional Prosecutor's Office.
The driver was detained and subsequently remanded in custody for two months by order of a Kaunas District Court.
This year, Customs Criminal Service officers have seized approximately 2.6 million packs of illegal cigarettes, mostly arriving from Latvia. Their total value, including mandatory taxes, is estimated at 13 million euros.

Relations between Lithuania and China soured in 2021 after Lithuania allowed Taiwan to open a representative office in Vilnius under the name "Taiwanese."

Estonia to ban new dangerous cannabis substances  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:35:04 UTC
23:35:04 KST

TALLINN - The Ministry of Social Affairs is adding the group of semi-synthetic cannabinoids to the list of narcotic and psychotropic substances to curb the spread and availability of these dangerous substances and prevent the health problems they cause.
Henceforth, all activities related to this substance group-such as possession, mediation, consumption, cultivation, manufacturing, storage, keeping, import, and export-will be prohibited in Estonia. The change primarily affects individuals who order semi-synthetic cannabinoids from abroad or use them, as well as companies that have been selling these products. The amendment will take effect on August 14 of this year.
The amendment will also affect the work of the Police and Border Guard Board and the Tax and Customs Board, as it will allow for a faster response to the discovery of new semi-synthetic cannabinoids and their removal from the market.
"New semi-synthetic cannabinoids are entering the market very quickly, and this is a serious problem that needs to be addressed. Whereas until now these substances have been banned one by one, we are now banning the entire substance group. This allows us to prevent the problem from worsening, react more quickly to the spread of new dangerous substances, and better protect public health," said Kristiin Mikko, an advisor at the Public Health Department.
She added that the use of these narcotic substances carries serious health risks, including poisoning, anxiety, mental health disorders, and cardiac arrhythmias.
Semi-synthetic cannabinoids are chemically modified forms of cannabinoids found in the cannabis plant that mimic the effects of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC); however, this category does not include CBD products (such as CBD-containing oils and teas). Semi-synthetic cannabinoids appeared on the European market in 2022 and began to be sold as a legal alternative to cannabis and THC. While initially there were only a few such substances, by the end of 2024, 24 different semi-synthetic cannabinoids had already been identified on the European drug market.
These substances are distributed in various forms: in e-cigarette liquids, as cannabis flowers or substances sprayed onto them, in herbal mixtures, as resin-like products, and in sweets, such as gummies and chocolates. Their inclusion in sweets is particularly concerning as it increases the risk of accidental poisoning among children.
In Estonia, semi-synthetic cannabinoids have also been found in the possession of private individuals and in postal shipments from abroad.
Until now, Estonia has added individual semi-synthetic cannabinoids to the list of narcotic and psychotropic substances. As new substances continuously enter the market, banning the entire substance group will allow for a faster response, more effectively curb their spread, and ultimately reduce related health damage and crime.
Semi-synthetic cannabinoids are chemically modified compounds that mimic the effects of THC. They entered the European market in 2022. By the end of 2024, 24 different semi-synthetic cannabinoids had already been identified on the European drug market. In Estonia, they have been discovered both in the possession of private individuals and in postal shipments. Adding the entire group of semi-synthetic cannabinoids to the list of narcotic and psychotropic substances will allow for a quicker and more effective curbing of the spread of new dangerous substances.

July in Financial Markets: Geopolitical Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher, Tech Sell-Off Shakes Asia  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:35:02 UTC
23:35:02 KST

Whatever relief markets drew from June's U.S.-Iran peace deal proved short lived. The truce collapsed on 8 July, and by mid-month Brent, which opened the month at a four-month low of USD 71.57, touched nearly USD 101 on July 23 before a late-month pause in strikes pulled it back to around USD 88, its strongest month since March. Yet the epicenter of July's market drama lay not in the Gulf but in Seoul, where the memory concentration risk we have already flagged finally crystallized: the KOSPI suffered its worst month since the 1997 Asian financial crisis, before staging the largest single day rally in its history on the final trading day.
The S&P 500 finished the month essentially flat at 0.1%, the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% due to the AI trade, while the Dow eked out a 0.3% gain, its fourth consecutive winning month. Europe again proved the quiet outperformer: carried by a solid earnings season, the STOXX 600 gained 1.5% and touched a record high on July 31 to secure a fourth straight monthly gain.
Korea pays the price of concentration
The Korean market, structurally "bipolar" with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix at roughly half the KOSPI's value, became July's defining story. Record margin balances concentrated in the very names falling fastest turned correction into rout, with more than 1.2m leveraged accounts (roughly 1 in 30 Korean adults) hit by margin calls and the Bank of Korea's first-rate hike since 2023, on 16 July, tightening liquidity into the forced selling. Only in the final week, the index already 27% below its June peak, did Chinese DUV lithography production and CXMT's Shanghai IPO challenge the assumption of Korean memory dominance, driving a capitulation that tripped circuit breakers on consecutive days for the first time in the index's history and left the KOSPI down 22.2% for the month. However, after Microsoft and Amazon confirmed AI infrastructure demand remains structurally undersupplied, the index surged a record 17.9%, with SK Hynix hitting its 30% daily limit. Notably, fundamentals never confirmed the panic as Korean chip exports surged 179% YoY to USD 41b in July.
Japan catches Korea's cold
Tokyo suffered a milder strain of the same virus. With AI and semiconductor heavyweights having dominated the index's advance through June, Japan could not sidestep the unwind even with a weakening yen at its back: the Nikkei fell roughly 8.7%, its first monthly loss in five months, after touching record highs near 72,000. The heaviest casualty was memory chip maker Kioxia, which collapsed 48% to less than half its June peak.
The BoJ held its policy rate at 1%, its highest since 1995, but the real action was in the currency. The yen had slid to 164 per dollar, a 40-year low and its weakest since 1986, before Tokyo mounted an estimated JPY 8.45t of yen-buying on July 30, likely the largest single-day intervention in its history, came with rare public backing from Washington, where Treasury Secretary Bessent called the yen “very undervalued”.
Earnings keep the AI story alive
By month-end, 61% of S&P 500 companies had reported Q2 results: 86% beat EPS estimates, the highest share since Q2 2021, while 77% topped revenue forecasts on top-line growth of about 14%. Headline blended earnings growth of 47.4% YoY flatters reality, inflated by Alphabet's one-off USD 98b gain; excluding it and Amazon (USD 53b), growth falls to a still remarkable 28.8%, a seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit gains.
Microsoft jumped 16% on Azure's results, Amazon surged over 15% on AWS growth even at some USD 220b in CapEx, while Meta fell 9% on the cash flow cost of its spending and Apple lost 7% on chip shortages. In Europe, roughly half of early STOXX 600 reporters beat estimates, with EPS growth near 18% YoY.
Holding rates, hardening tone
While equities obsessed over chips, July's more consequential repricing may have happened in Treasuries. The 30-year yield spiked to 5.25%, its highest since 2007, and the 10-year pushed past 4.7%. Both the Fed and the ECB held, and neither felt dovish: the FOMC kept its range at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote, with three dissenters preferring an immediate hike, the first such split since 2016, while the ECB, after June's 25bp pivot back to tightening, held at 2.25% on July 23 with a September 10 hike all but promised. As of month-end, markets priced roughly 60% odds of a September Fed hike and a near fully priced ECB move to 2.50%.

First phase of Rail Baltica main line in Latvia is planned within current scope, with significant optimization  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:34:55 UTC
23:34:55 KST

RIGA - The first phase of Rail Baltica railway project in Latvia is planned within the current scope, which calls for establishing a Rail Baltica cross-border connection from Lithuania to the Estonian border, as well as to complete construction work at the Riga Airport and the southern section of the Riga Central Train Terminal to ensure the connection between Rail Baltica and the existing railway network, Transport Minister Rihards Kozlovskis (New Unity) told the media on Wednesday following a meeting of the thematic committee on Rail Baltica project implementation.
The minister emphasized that this is a solution for the first phase of the project and that the idea of the "Riga Circle" remains a part of the project. "We would like to look at it differently, but it is 2026 and we have to think rationally," the minister stressed.
He reported that on Wednesday, the committee heard a presentation on the results of the in-depth assessment of the Rail Baltica project, which outlined three scenarios.
"One scenario was to continue as before, which is neither supportable nor feasible. The second scenario is to reassess and scale back the requirements, while the third scenario is to immediately halt any further activities," Kozlovskis explained.
He emphasized that the focus should be on optimizing the project - that is, building and financing only what is technically necessary, rather than "funding various visions and, to a certain extent, dreams."
Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List) noted that Latvia must establish a "minimum program," or base scenario. He said that in their assessment, the consultants concluded that, for example, on the 600-kilometer high-speed rail section between Madrid and Barcelona, there are technically two stations, but only one is primarily used, whereas in Latvia, 17 stations are planned for a 200-kilometer section. He also noted that the planned length of station platforms is 400 meters, but technically this can be reduced to 200 meters.
The Prime Minister stated that the Ministry of Transport must develop proposals by September 15 to reduce the technical and construction material requirements for the within the current scope of the first phase to reduce technical and construction material requirements to the minimum necessary for the creation of a functional and permanently operational railway line. "So we are going down to the bare minimum to understand what we can build and what we cannot," Kulbergs emphasized.
He added that, taking into account the proposals provided in the consultant’s assessment regarding the project’s cost estimates, the Ministry of Finance and the State Treasury, the Ministry of Transport, and the Ministry of Economics must, by September 15, assess the potential scope of state budget funding for the implementation of Rail Baltica in the coming years, as well as other sources of funding and opportunities to attract investment.
He explained that the law currently stipulates that the Rail Baltica project involves military mobility, making it possible to secure military funding - a possibility that had not been explicitly provided for until now. "We need to think outside the box to see what other options exist, because Europe will not provide enough money in the next budget to carry out this project," Kulbergs emphasized.
The third task, meanwhile, calls for the State Chancellery, in cooperation with the Ministry of Transport, to evaluate the project management changes proposed by the consultant. Kulbergs stressed that management has not been effective so far, as the state’s interests are not being defended in negotiations with the contractors.
He stressed that the contract for the construction of the main line, signed in December 2023, has "put us in a bind," as it was concluded without verification by experts or project documentation. According to him, this contract does not set a maximum ceiling, as there are no defined upper limits on what Latvia can afford.
"This is a good contractor who can build it, but the question is whether we can afford it. This contractor charges a very substantial amount every month. If we continue to build as we have so far, no one will know when it will be ready or how to finance it. Likewise, no one will be able to afford to buy a train ticket," Kulbergs emphasized.
As reported, in accordance with a decision by the Cabinet of Ministers, an in-depth assessment of Rail Baltica project was launched on November 3 of last year, conducted by the international consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal.
The value of the contract is confidential.
The purpose of the assessment is to obtain an objective and comprehensive analysis of the implementation of Rail Baltica project, to conduct an in-depth examination of the risks, the financial and contractual status, and to develop recommendations and a practical action plan for the project’s future effective, transparent, and sustainable implementation.
It was also reported that, at the end of July this year, the government established a thematic committee for the implementation of Rail Baltica, comprising ten members of the government. It was established to ensure, under the leadership of the Prime Minister, cross-sectoral consultation and coordination among government members regarding the systematic, technically functional, and financially sound future implementation of the Rail Baltica project.
As reported, according to project implementer RB Rail, the cost of the first phase of the Rail Baltica project in the Baltics could reach EUR 14.3 billion, including EUR 5.5 billion in Latvia.
The total cost of the project could reach EUR 23.8 billion in the Baltics, according to the cost-benefit analysis. A previous cost-benefit analysis in 2017 estimated the total cost of the project at EUR 5.8 billion.
The Rail Baltica project will build a European standard gauge railway line from Tallinn to the Lithuanian-Polish border to connect the Baltic States with other European countries by rail.

Russia publishes list of 224 Ukrainian POWs it says it is ready to swap amid dispute with Kyiv
LONDON, Aug 12 - Russia's human rights commissioner published on Wednesday a list of 224 Ukrainian prisoners of war that she said Moscow was ready to exchange but that Kyiv had rejected, part of a dispute over which side is hampering exchange efforts.
Thousands of prisoners have been exchanged since the start of the full-scale war in February 2022. An agreement in May to swap a further 1,000 captives each was one of the main tangible results of U.S.-brokered peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine.
A number of exchanges have taken place since then, but on Monday "I Want to Find", a Ukrainian government-backed project that tracks the status of captured or killed Russian soldiers, accused Moscow of excluding from exchange lists POWs from Russian-held territory in Ukraine.
Denying the allegation in a video statement, Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova said Russia did not discriminate against those from Russian-held parts of Ukraine's Donetsk and Luhansk regions.
"For our part, we are ready for an exchange," she said in a statement, saying Russia had proposed three different lists of potential candidates for a swap to Ukraine over the past month. "But Ukraine is refusing to take back its own citizens."
Her statement linked to a list of 224 Ukrainians she said Kyiv had most recently declined to exchange.
Ukraine's parliamentary commissioner for human rights, Dmytro Lubinets, said the claim that Ukraine had rejected proposed swaps was "cynical lies".
"Ukraine is always committed to bringing back every one of its citizens—and works toward this goal every day," he said on the Telegram messaging app on Wednesday.
Neither side publishes comprehensive figures for the number of prisoners of war it holds and both accuse the other of abuses.
On Monday, a U.N. human rights official said U.N. monitoring showed ongoing "widespread and systematic torture and ill-treatment of Ukrainian prisoners of war and civilian detainees by the Russian Federation authorities."
The monitoring had also documented torture and ill-treatment of Russian POWs held by Ukraine, but "on a fundamentally different scale,” the official said at an informal Security Council meeting.
Russia's representative at the meeting rejected the allegations against it. REUTERS

Hungary to build Danube weir to protect Paks nuclear plant
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
22:34:38 CST
23:34:38 KST

BUDAPEST, Aug. 12 (Xinhua) -- The Hungarian government has ordered the immediate construction of a submerged weir on the Danube to prevent extremely low water levels from disrupting operations at the Paks nuclear power plant, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Wednesday.
Speaking after an on-site government meeting at the plant, Magyar said construction would begin on Thursday between Paks and Dunaszentbenedek, initially using 35,000 cubic meters of rock and later increasing to 110,000 cubic meters.
The structure is designed to prevent the Danube's water level at the plant's cooling-water channel from falling below minus 90 centimeters and could eventually raise the local water level by as much as one meter, according to Magyar.
As a temporary emergency measure, the government also ordered two 80-meter barges to be placed on standby at Paks. Magyar said the barges could, if necessary, be deliberately sunk across the river to temporarily raise the water level by up to 20 centimeters until the permanent structure is completed.
A final decision on whether to use the barges is expected on Friday, he said.
The announcement came after the Danube's water level rose temporarily in recent days, allowing the Paks plant to begin increasing its output on Monday.
However, Magyar said water-management forecasts indicated that the river could fall again to around minus 136 to minus 137 centimeters within four to five days and could drop below minus 140 centimeters next week without intervention, potentially again threatening the plant's operation.
He said no significant rainfall was expected in the Danube catchment area in the coming days and weeks, meaning extremely low water levels could persist for months.
The government estimated the cost of the interventions at around 6 billion forints (about 18 million U.S. dollars), while a complete shutdown of Paks would cost the state budget at least 50 billion forints per month, Magyar said.
Around 100 soldiers have been deployed to assist with the project, with work planned around the clock. Magyar said the government would classify the project as a priority investment because of its urgency.
The Paks nuclear power plant, located about 100 km south of Budapest, is Hungary's only commercial nuclear power facility and accounts for a significant share of the country's electricity generation. ■

BEIJING, Aug. 12 (Xinhua) -- China will strengthen financial support for key areas, including expanding domestic demand, promoting technological innovation and supporting small and micro enterprises, according to a report released by the People's Bank of China (PBOC) Wednesday.

====================================================================================================

Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji passes away at 98
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
22:34:27 CST
23:34:27 KST

A file photo of Zhu Rongji. Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji died of illness at the age of 98 in Beijing at 11:06 a.m. Wednesday. (Xinhua)
BEIJING, Aug. 12 (Xinhua) -- Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji died of illness at the age of 98 in Beijing at 11:06 a.m. Wednesday.
Zhu had served as a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the 14th and 15th Central Committees of the Communist Party of China (CPC).
An obituary, jointly issued by the CPC Central Committee, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the State Council and the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, extolled Zhu as an excellent Party member, a time-tested and loyal communist fighter, and an outstanding proletarian revolutionist, statesman and leader of the Party and the state.
Zhu was born in October 1928 in Changsha, central China's Hunan Province. He studied in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Tsinghua University from 1947 to 1951. He joined the CPC in October 1949.
From 1951 to 1983, Zhu worked at various places and held a series of posts related to economic affairs in regional and central government departments and institutions. He served as deputy director of the now-defunct State Economic Commission from 1983 to 1987.
Between 1987 and 1991, he served successively as deputy secretary of the CPC Shanghai Municipal Committee, mayor of Shanghai, and secretary of the CPC Shanghai Municipal Committee.
In Shanghai, he urged the municipality to readjust its industrial structure, cultivate new development strengths, enhance its international competitiveness, and pursue an export-oriented development path.
In 1991, Zhu was appointed vice premier of the State Council.
In October 1992, Zhu was elected a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and its standing committee, and took charge of the State Council's day-to-day work.
In June 1993, he concurrently served as the governor of the People's Bank of China.
He actively championed the implementation of the principles outlined in Deng Xiaoping's remarks during Deng's 1992 southern China tour and worked hard to promote reform and opening up as well as China's modernization drive.
He organized campaigns to resolve the problem of debt chains known as the "triangular debts."
Also, he studied and developed approaches and measures to strengthen and improve macroeconomic regulation, making significant and effective contributions to curbing an overheated economy, reining in inflation and achieving an economic "soft landing."
He pushed forward efforts to rectify and restore order in the fiscal and taxation sectors, accelerated fiscal and tax reforms and helped improve China's financial regulation system.
In September 1997, Zhu was re-elected a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and its standing committee.
In March 1998, Zhu was appointed premier of the State Council. Facing the impact of the Asian financial crisis and the catastrophic flooding in China, he implemented the plans of the Party Central Committee to shift from a moderately tight fiscal and monetary policy to a proactive fiscal policy and a prudent monetary policy, expand domestic demand and deepen reforms in key areas, thereby sustaining steady and rapid economic growth.
He introduced a series of policies and measures to broaden opening up and encourage exports, while firmly preventing the devaluation of the renminbi. He also took measures to actively attract foreign investment and better utilize both domestic and international markets and resources, and firmly safeguarded the prosperity and stability of Hong Kong as an international financial center.
Zhu worked to establish the basic living security system for laid-off workers from state-owned enterprises, the unemployment insurance system, and the minimum living guarantee system for urban residents. He also made great efforts to address issues such as wage arrears and the re-employment of laid-off workers.
During Zhu's tenure as vice premier and premier of the State Council, China was in a critical period of transitioning from a planned economy to a socialist market economy.
Under the firm leadership of the CPC Central Committee with Jiang Zemin at the core, Zhu spearheaded reform of the fiscal and taxation systems, carrying out a major overhaul of the tax regime centered on fairer tax burdens and a simplified tax system. He introduced a tax sharing system based on a rational division of fiscal responsibilities between the central and local governments, and launched pilot reforms of taxes and fees in rural areas. He actively promoted the reform of the financial system, further regulated the functions of the central bank, deepened reforms of commercial banks, the foreign exchange system, and the securities and futures markets, and promoted the establishment of a nationally unified and open financial market system with orderly competition and strict regulation.
Zhu took the reform of state-owned enterprises as the central link of economic structural reform. He stressed that every effort must be made to promote the re-employment of laid-off workers and strengthen the social security system.
He advanced housing reform, gradually replacing the allocation of housing to employees with monetary housing benefits. He helped establish and improve a multi-level urban housing supply system with economically affordable housing as the main component.
He also promoted the establishment of the basic framework for a socialist market economy, oversaw the completion of the arduous negotiations for China's accession to the World Trade Organization, and advanced the country's opening up in both scope and depth.
Zhu had deep affection for the people. He emphasized that government officials must always bear in mind that they are public servants and should have the courage to speak the truth, not fear giving offense, and refrain from seeking special privileges, the obituary said.
He stressed the need to take the initiative, with a strong sense of responsibility, to shoulder heavy burdens, take on tough problems and go all out to deliver real results for the people, it added.
In March 2003, Zhu no longer served as premier of the State Council.
After retiring from leadership posts, he steadfastly upheld and supported the CPC Central Committee with Hu Jintao as general secretary, and then the CPC Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. He continued to care about the great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics and firmly supported efforts to improve conduct, promote integrity and fight corruption.
Zhu's life was a revolutionary, fighting and glorious one. His death is a great loss to the Party and the state, the obituary said.
Eternal glory to Zhu, it added. ■

A 141-meter ship mysteriously “disappeared” in the Black Sea near Novorossiysk, while Russian authorities are keeping the incident under wraps
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
14:34:09 UTC
23:34:09 KST

Overnight on 7 August, a vessel was possibly sunk in the Black Sea near Novorossiysk, the Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ reports. The project, which spotted the ship in satellite imagery, suggests it may have been carrying military cargo.
Russia has a practice of concealing its fleet losses. Moscow tries to mask the scale of the problem in various ways: it classifies sinkings as accidents, downplays the number of casualties, or stays completely silent about vessel losses. Russia acknowledges fleet losses only when it happens accidentally or when concealing the sinking or damage is no longer possible. The 141-meter vessel, which had no foreign owner to demand explanations, has received none.
Russian officials have not commented on the sinking, Exilenova+ says.
"The news passed quite modestly, but there is a nuance. Russia's 'official' authorities have not reported about any sunken vessel. It just sank. It is not ruled out that the ship was carrying military cargo for Russia's armed forces. Otherwise, why pretend nothing happened?" Exilenova+ wrote.
The vessel was approximately 141 meters long, suggesting a displacement of roughly 10,000 tonnes, according to the Ukrainian outlet Militarnyi.
The strikes that may have caused the sinking
Over 48 hours on 6-7 August, the Unmanned Systems Forces (SBS) struck 102 enemy targets, SBS Commander Robert “Madyar” Brovdi reported. In the same post, he noted that the targets included six shadow fleet vessels in the Black and Azov Seas: two tankers and four dry cargo ships. The SBS also reported striking three units of Russia's fleet on 7 August alone.
"It is entirely possible that the vessel that sank near Novorossiysk is among those struck in those days”, Militarnyi suggests.
Novorossiysk under fire again on 12 August
Just hours after the news of the earlier reported sinking surfaced publicly, Novorossiysk came under attack. Overnight on 12 August, Ukraine's defense forces conducted what President Zelenskyy called a "unique operation" against the naval base, using Palianytsia jet drones, Neptune missiles, and unmanned naval systems.
Novorossiysk became Russia's primary Black Sea naval hub after Ukrainian strikes forced the fleet out of Sevastopol.

Namibia's central bank keeps repo rate unchanged at 6.75 pct
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
22:33:52 CST
23:33:52 KST

WINDHOEK, Aug. 12 (Xinhua) -- Namibia's central bank on Wednesday kept its benchmark repo rate unchanged at 6.75 percent, balancing subdued domestic economic activity against inflationary pressures and the need to safeguard the country's currency peg.
Bank of Namibia Governor Ebson Uanguta said the decision was appropriate to support international reserves and maintain the one-to-one peg between the Namibia dollar and the South African rand.
Domestic economic activity remained weak during the first half of 2026, with sluggish performance in mining, manufacturing, electricity generation and transport, while agriculture and wholesale and retail trade improved, he said.
Annual private-sector credit growth slowed to 4.5 percent in June, mainly due to lower credit uptake by businesses. Meanwhile, annual headline inflation rose to 4.4 percent in June from 4.1 percent in May, primarily driven by higher transport prices.
Namibia's merchandise trade deficit widened to 19.3 billion Namibian dollars (about 1.2 billion U.S. dollars) in the first half of 2026 from 12.8 billion Namibian dollars in the same period last year, largely due to higher mineral fuel import payments.
The country's international reserves rose to 57.1 billion Namibian dollars at the end of July, equivalent to an estimated 3.5 months of import cover and sufficient to support the currency peg and meet international financial obligations, the bank said. ■

Mozambique approves payment mechanism to secure fuel imports
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
22:33:44 CST
23:33:44 KST

MAPUTO, Aug. 12 (Xinhua) -- The Mozambican government has approved an emergency financing mechanism to help secure fuel imports and maintain domestic supplies during periods of fuel crisis, the Mozambique News Agency reported Wednesday.
Under a resolution approved by the Council of Ministers, the mechanism will operate through state-owned fuel company Petromoc, using an account held by the Ministry of Finance at the Bank of Mozambique, the country's central bank.
According to the resolution, the finance minister, in coordination with the minister responsible for fuels, may authorize the use of up to 50 million U.S. dollars under the payment facility to ensure the import of liquid fuels for the domestic market in the event of a supply crisis.
Under the arrangement, Petromoc will have access to the account, enabling it to make payments to foreign fuel suppliers on behalf of qualifying importers.
The measure comes amid renewed concerns over fuel shortages in parts of the country following supply disruptions in April and May, which led to long queues at filling stations in Maputo and other cities.
Mozambican authorities have attributed the supply difficulties to disruptions in international fuel trade linked to tensions in the Middle East, as well as financial difficulties faced by some fuel distributors and foreign currency shortages. ■

"This offensive operation of ours has been carried out precisely - exactly as planned," the president said.
In total, control was restored over 12 settlements in Dnipropetrovsk region, 10 in Donetsk region and four in Zaporizhia region during the offensive, and search-and-destroy operations were conducted against enemy forces that had infiltrated the rear area across more than 300 square kilometers, the Air Assault Forces command reported.
"Units and subunits of Ukraine’s Air Assault Forces have taken control of the settlements of Tolstoy, Novokhatske, Hrushivske, Zirka, Zelenyi Hai, Piddubne, Myrne, Tsehelne, Pryvillia, Zlahoda, Krasnohirske, Pryvilne, Novohryhorivka, Stepove, Kalynivske, Berezove, Novomykolaivka, Voskresenka, Oleksandrohrad and Yalta. Units and subunits of Ukraine’s Assault Forces have taken control of the settlements of Rybne, Maliivka, Sichneve, Ternove, Novoheorhiivka and Zaporizke," the command said on its Telegram channel.
The Air Assault Forces command said the operation’s success was made possible by careful planning at the strategic, operational and tactical levels, effective staff work, all types of reconnaissance, continuous collection and analysis of information on the enemy, quality training of personnel, skillful organization of fire support and logistics, and clear coordination among all elements of the grouping.
"Every stage of the operation was planned down to the smallest detail. Coordinated work by staffs, reconnaissance, joint fire support units and assault groups made it possible to retain the initiative, impose our own tempo of battle on the enemy, and successfully accomplish the combat tasks assigned," said DSHV commander Oleh Apostol.
The core of the strike grouping consisted of Air Assault Forces units, which, together with Assault Forces subunits and other components of Ukraine’s Defense Forces, successfully broke through enemy defenses, overcame resistance and accomplished the assigned combat tasks.
"Ukrainian soldiers are currently continuing to build on the success of the offensive operation and are methodically destroying the combat potential of the Russian occupation forces," the DSHV command said.

Italy's brutal heatwaves have so far
driven a 20% rise in the number of emergency room visits for
mental-health issues this summer, Italian health bodies said
Wednesday.
                                    
                                       
				"This summer's extreme heat has also caused up to a 20% increase
in visits for psychiatric disorders to some Italian emergency
rooms compared to three years ago," said a statement by Simeu
(Italian Society of Emergency Medicine) and SIEP (Italian
Society of Psychiatric Epidemiology), confirming that the
phenomenon is not marginal but structural.
                                    
                                       
				Extreme heat, the statement emphasizes, can aggravate anxiety,
mood disorders, and other psychiatric conditions, and promote
psychotic disorders, depressive episodes, and self-harm.
                                    
                                       
				For this reason, the two societies are calling for people with
mental disorders to be explicitly recognized among vulnerable
groups in national heatwave prevention plans.
                                    
                                       
				A special role In this context, Simeu and Siep explain,
psychotropic drug therapies are at risk: the real
pharmacological risk concerns molecules with anticholinergic
action, which inhibit sweating, but the greatest danger remains
improper or self-managed discontinuation of therapies, a major
cause of relapse.
                                    
                                       
				Social isolation and housing insecurity also contribute to
making people with mental disorders more vulnerable, with homes
often lacking air conditioning or adequate thermal insulation.

The UK government is considering banning disposable barbecues to help prevent wildfires during the country's extreme summer heat, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Wednesday.
Speaking to reporters during a visit to Stevenage, Burnham said he is "certainly going to consider" a ban.
“There is obviously a significant problem of wildfires in the south,” Burnham said. “The New Forest fire is a great concern; we have seen them in northern areas, as well as Suffolk recently.”
He said many of the wildfires had been caused by disposable barbecues and urged the public not to use them outdoors under the current conditions.
“I do believe we need to get the message out loud and clear. People should not be using those barbecues outside at this moment in time,” he said.

“I don’t know yet what the remedy is, but I do want to leave the meeting today with a loud and clear message that we do want people to take the greatest possible care when they are out in the countryside, both in terms of cigarettes, but also those temporary barbecues that we know are causing risk of fires,” he said.
The UK's Met Office said Tuesday the country is on course to record its hottest summer on record for average temperature if average conditions continue through the rest of August.
Heat health alerts have been upgraded across England ahead of soaring temperatures, with highs of up to 36 C (96.8 F) forecast in southeast England on Thursday.
More than two-thirds of England is officially in drought after the country recorded its driest July since records began in 1836.
Last month, the UK Health Security Agency said Britain recorded 2,877 excess deaths during the May and June heat waves, nearly double the 1,504 excess deaths recorded during the summer of 2025.

Lebanon passes long-sought amnesty law, a day after death penalty repeal

Lebanon passes long-sought amnesty law, a day after death penalty repeal
The legislation will ‘exceptionally’ reduce certain prison terms, says Lebanon’s parliament speaker.
Lebanon’s parliament has approved a general amnesty law that is expected to benefit thousands of convicted prisoners, detainees and wanted people.
The legislation passed Wednesday in a “show-of-hands vote”, reported Lebanon’s official National News Agency. It is the first law of its kind since 1991.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Lebanon ‘files new lawsuit against’ ex-central bank chief Riad Salameh
- list 2 of 3Bashar al-Assad, Atef Najib sentenced to death in landmark Syria trial
- list 3 of 3Lebanese soldiers injured while Israeli troops intrude on southern town
The office of the country’s parliament speaker said the law would “exceptionally” reduce certain prison terms.
Long demanded by numerous Lebanese political factions, the amnesty law aims to reduce overcrowding in prisons, where many inmates await trial for years.
However, it has faced backlash from some family members of Lebanese soldiers and servicemen killed in attacks, who fear the perpetrators could receive undue leniency.
Lebanese authorities did not immediately announce the number of people who would be freed or receive reduced sentences under the law, which comes a day after Lebanon’s parliament also formally abolished the death penalty.
According to Imad al-Hout, one of the lawmakers in favour of the bill, the law reduced the sentences of those facing death and life imprisonment to 17 “prison years”.
That is equivalent to 12 years and nine months of actual imprisonment in Lebanon, where a prison year is calculated as nine months.
The law also calls for the release of inmates in ongoing trials who have been detained for more than 12 prison years without charges.
In its 2025 report, the country’s National Human Rights Commission said that prisons had an overcrowding rate of 300 percent, with prison authorities reporting at least 6,268 inmates by the end of March.
‘Long-awaited’
A push for general amnesty grew after the 2024 fall of longtime Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, as Lebanon jailed many prisoners over events linked to the Syrian civil war.
Most of those prisoners hail from northern Lebanon’s Sunni-majority city Tripoli and are accused of crimes that include attacking the Lebanese army, participating in clashes and planning bombings.
Other political forces, including the Iran-backed Shia movement Hezbollah, have been demanding amnesty for their communities.
Thousands of families from the eastern Baalbek and Hermel regions, bastions of Hezbollah and its ally Amal, where illicit cannabis cultivation is widespread, have been demanding amnesty for drug-related offences and car theft for years.
Christian parties, meanwhile, pushed for an amnesty law to include the families of those who joined an Israeli-backed group and fled to Israel after its withdrawal from southern Lebanon in 2000, fearing reprisals, particularly from Hezbollah and its supporters.
Deputy Walid Baarini praised the “long-awaited passage” of the amnesty law and expressed hope it would mark “a new chapter” that brings justice “to those who deserve it”.
“Amnesty is not forgetting a right, but rather prioritising mercy and wisdom when they align with the requirements of justice and the national interest,” he wrote in a post on X.
Lebanon previously passed a general amnesty law in the wake of its 1975-90 civil war.

The Juozas Miltinis Drama Theatre in Panevėžys has cancelled scheduled performances of Macbeth after failing to reach an agreement with lead actor Tadas Gryn on the terms of a new contract.
The dispute has also raised concerns about other productions featuring Gryn, prompting Culture Minister Lukas Alsys to meet with the theatre’s management. Theatre officials acknowledged that communication errors contributed to the situation.
About 1,200 theatregoers were left without tickets to the cancelled performances of Aleksandr Špilevoj’s production of“Macbeth. All scheduled shows had been sold out.
Gryn ended his employment contract with the theatre after the sides failed to agree on terms for continuing their collaboration. He also appears in several other productions in the theatre’s repertoire.
“The theatre acknowledged that perhaps there were mistakes in communication and that talks with the actor began too late,” Alsys said after meeting with theatre officials. He added that the theatre was making every effort to reach an agreement with Gryn.
Culture Vice Minister Tomas Juočys, who previously headed the Klaipėda Drama Theatre for several years, described the dispute as a communication breakdown that should have been resolved internally.
“I have never done that publicly and never will. If I want to talk to someone, I will do so,” Juočys said, referring to the handling of the dispute.
Theatre director Antanas Venckus acknowledged that management waited too long to negotiate a new agreement with Gryn after the actor decided to leave his permanent position.
“I feel that I may have made a mistake by trusting his assurance that he would perform the already announced shows after leaving his position,” Venckus said. “Perhaps I should have interrupted my vacation and tried to start negotiations earlier.”
Asked whether the disagreement was about money or other contractual terms, Venckus said there were no other issues.
“It is also a condition,” he said of the fee.
Gryn, however, said money was not the main issue and that the dispute was primarily about the lack of communication.
“As for the mysterious money, the narrative about money – that’s not the point,” Gryn said. “From the beginning, I communicated that it was about the inability to talk. Negotiations are a normal process. We have to agree on terms – terms that work for them and terms that work for me.”
Gryn said he had tried to initiate discussions himself, including by calling the theatre’s director, but received what he described as a dismissal rather than an invitation to negotiate.
He also criticised the Culture Ministry for meeting only with theatre management.
“It is a little disappointing that the ministry called only the management, only one side, and did not invite me to the meeting,” Gryn said. “In my view, both sides should be heard.”
The theatre’s artistic director, Paulius Pinigis, said he was working to prevent further disruption to the repertoire.
“I am now communicating both with Tadas and with the directors whose productions he performs in. We are trying to find a way to communicate and save the repertoire,” Pinigis said.
The theatre’s new season is scheduled to begin in early September. One of the first productions, The Island That Doesn’t Exist, is scheduled for September 9 and features Gryn.
Venckus said the theatre hopes to avoid further changes to its repertoire and reach a mutually acceptable agreement with the actor.

Goods worth an amount equal to the annual budget of a large Russian region burned down at Wildberries warehouses — analysts
Kyiv • UNN
Ukrainian Armed Forces strikes on Wildberries warehouses caused losses of 480 billion rubles, exceeding the annual budget of the Irkutsk region. The marketplace lost a third of its warehouse capacity, while the Russian government does not plan direct payments to sellers.
The damage from Ukrainian Armed Forces attacks on Wildberries warehouses, at least 12 of which were mega-hubs that burned almost completely to the ground, continues to grow. According to analysts, goods worth 480 billion rubles have now been destroyed—a sum comparable to the annual budgets of large and wealthy Russian regions, UNN reports, citing The Moscow Times.
Details
Russia’s largest marketplace, Wildberries, which has nearly one hundred thousand order pickup points and sells 6 trillion rubles’ worth of goods annually, has currently lost one-third of its warehouse capacity, analysts at Data Insight estimate.
According to analysts’ calculations, goods worth 480 billion rubles burned in the warehouses hit by the attacks—a sum comparable to the annual budgets of large and wealthy Russian regions such as Krasnoyarsk Krai (527 billion rubles) or the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug (476 billion rubles). The annual budget of Irkutsk Oblast, for example (303 billion rubles), was exceeded by the losses from the attacks on Wildberries by 1.6 times; the annual budget of Smolensk or Penza Oblast by almost four times; and the budgets of Kalmykia, the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, or the Nenets Autonomous Okrug by 14–17 times.
In addition
Wildberries has "practically no large warehouses left," Data Insight analyst Sergey Semko told The New York Times: "Every day, one warehouse after another is methodically destroyed." The Russian government is preparing a package for sellers who lost goods, but it does not include direct payments to those affected. Payment holidays, preferential loans, and tax relief are being considered. The Russian budget currently does not have the hundreds of billions of rubles needed to help sellers, a source close to the Kremlin told Reuters.
